Name: Farmer's End - Escalating Combat and Dungeon Difficulty
Author: acharles1
Description:
[center][b][size=6]Farmer’s End[/size][/b][/center]
[center][i]The farther you push, the harder the expedition pushes back.[/i][/center]

[center]Every expedition starts quietly.[/center]
[center]A few monsters.[/center]
[center]A few fights.[/center]
[center]A few more floors.[/center]
[center]Then the pressure starts to build.[/center]
[center]The farther you push, the harder the expedition pushes back.[/center]
[center]And if you keep going long enough...[/center]
[center]you may eventually reach [b]Farmer’s End[/b].[/center]
[center]
[color=#f1c232][size=1][font=Verdana][b]A little support goes a long way.[/b][/font][/size][/color]
[color=#f1c232][size=1][font=Verdana][b] Endorsements, comments, and feedback help these mods grow and inspire what comes next.[/b][/font][/size][/color]
[color=#f1c232][size=1][font=Verdana][b] Thanks for being part of it.[/b][/font][/size][/color]
[/center]



⚔ [b]WHAT IS FARMER’S END?[/b]
[b]Farmer’s End[/b] is an expedition-based combat pressure system for the Mines, Skull Cavern, Volcano, and other eligible progression areas available through Stardew Valley’s normal runtime systems.
Threat is based on how far you progress during a single expedition, not the absolute floor you start on.
Start deep? Things are still calm.
Keep pushing?
That’s when the expedition begins to escalate.


🌋 [b]NEW IN V1.1 — RUMBLE[/b]
High-threat expeditions can now trigger [b]RUMBLE[/b] — a dangerous falling-rock event that turns the battlefield itself against you.
When a RUMBLE begins, the area starts shaking and rocks begin falling from above.
If a falling rock hits you:
[list]
[*][b]Hunted:[/b] 10 damage[/*]
[*][b]Insane:[/b] 20 damage[/*]
[*]The falling rock shatters on impact[/*]
[/list]If you dodge it, the rock lands and becomes a normal breakable mine rock.
RUMBLE doesn’t just threaten you while it’s happening. It can physically reshape the floor, reduce movement space, and make an already-dangerous expedition harder to navigate.


👹 [b]NOT JUST STRONGER MONSTERS[/b]
Farmer’s End does [b]not[/b] make every monster permanently stronger.
The challenge increases because [b]you keep pushing the same expedition[/b].
A fresh run starts calm.
Keep advancing, and the pressure builds through:
[list]
[*]More monsters[/*]
[*]Wider awareness and aggro[/*]
[*]Stronger pursuit[/*]
[*]Increased damage at higher threat[/*]
[*]Breach reinforcements[/*]
[*][b]MONSTER AMBUSH![/b][/*]
[*]RUMBLE[/*]
[*]And eventually [b]Farmer’s End Leaders[/b][/*]
[/list]The goal is not to turn every enemy into a damage sponge.
The difficulty comes from how far you push the expedition.


🗻 [b]THREAT STAGES[/b]
[b]Calm[/b] — Normal monster population and normal awareness.
[b]Stirring[/b] — More monsters begin appearing and nearby creatures start reacting sooner.
[b]Alert[/b] — Monster pressure increases and enemies notice you from farther away.
[b]Hunted[/b] — You are now actively being hunted. Monster numbers rise sharply, enemies focus on you from much greater distances, and monsters deal [b]15% more damage[/b].
[b]Insane[/b] — The expedition reaches maximum pressure. Monster density is at its highest, enemies deal [b]25% more damage[/b], reinforcements become stronger, and [b]Farmer’s End Leaders[/b] can emerge.


👺 [b]FARMER’S END LEADERS[/b]
At maximum threat, existing monsters can be promoted into [b]Farmer’s End Leaders[/b].
They become:
[list]
[*]Larger[/*]
[*]Tougher[/*]
[*]Harder to knock back[/*]
[*]Around 90% more health[/*]
[*]Around 35% more damage[/*]
[*]Slightly faster[/*]
[*]Permanently aware of the farmer[/*]
[*]Persistent in their pursuit[/*]
[*]Marked by a pulsing red glow[/*]
[/list]Once Farmer’s End appears, it begins coming for you.


🫨 [b]MONSTER AMBUSH![/b]
Sometimes monsters can become stranded in unreachable parts of a map — even in normal Stardew gameplay.
Farmer’s End turns that problem into part of the experience.
If normal ground monsters become genuinely embedded or unreachable, the system can recover the confirmed group and bring them back into the fight together.
[b]MONSTER AMBUSH![/b]


🎁 [b]REWARDS[/b]
Higher threat comes with modest extra rewards.
Defeating all Farmer’s End Leaders grants one additional area-appropriate reward.


🪛 [b]COMBAT OVERHAUL COMPATIBILITY[/b]
Farmer’s End does not replace Stardew Valley’s combat system.
Instead, it adds expedition pressure through:
[list]
[*]Threat progression[/*]
[*]Monster population[/*]
[*]Awareness and aggro[/*]
[*]Hunted / Insane damage pressure[/*]
[*]Breach reinforcements[/*]
[*]Leader promotion[/*]
[*]RUMBLE[/*]
[*]Bonus rewards[/*]
[/list]This allows Stardew’s existing combat behaviour to remain in place while Farmer’s End controls how strongly the expedition responds as you continue pushing forward.


🧌 [b]WHY I MADE FARMER’S END[/b]
I wanted a combat system that still felt like Stardew Valley.
I didn’t want every monster to suddenly become a giant health sponge, and I didn’t want combat difficulty to come from simply multiplying stats.
I wanted the Mines to start familiar and slowly become more dangerous the farther I pushed.
I wanted progression to feel earned, but not so fast that every run became disposable.
Most of all, I wanted mining to feel like an expedition worth diving into again and again.
A run should begin calmly.
Then build.
Then become dangerous.
And eventually reach the point where you have to decide:
[b]Do I leave now... or push one more floor?[/b]
That is what Farmer’s End is built around.
[b]In short:[/b]
The farther you push, the harder the expedition pushes back.
And if you keep going long enough...
you may eventually reach [b]Farmer’s End[/b].



📦 [b]REQUIREMENTS[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/b][/*]
[*][b]SMAPI 4.0+[/b][/*]
[*][b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] — Optional[/*]
[/list]

💡 [b]COMPATIBILITY / GAMEPLAY CLARIFICATION[/b]
Farmer’s End is built around [b]Stardew Valley and SMAPI’s normal runtime systems[/b] and does not depend on any other mod’s content.
Its expedition mechanics use gameplay information already available through Stardew Valley, including locations, monsters, floor progression, combat state, monster positioning, health, damage, and player progression during the current expedition.
[b]Farmer’s End applies temporary runtime modifiers to eligible monsters already loaded by the game[/b], such as health, damage, size, awareness, pursuit, and visual effects.
It does not edit, replace, or redistribute monster files, sprites, maps, code, assets, or other source content.
It applies its own predefined expedition rules to eligible monsters and areas available through Stardew Valley’s normal gameplay systems.
Farmer’s End also does not replace Stardew Valley’s core combat system. Its threat stages, damage modifiers, reinforcements, Leaders, RUMBLE events, and recovery systems are controlled by the mod’s own programmed rules.
[b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] is supported.

🤖 [b]AI DISCLOSURE[/b]
The [b]AI-Generated Content[/b] tag reflects the use of AI assistance during development of Farmer’s End, including development of the mod’s code.
The mod itself was designed, tested, balanced, adjusted, and assembled by me.
[b]Farmer’s End uses vanilla Stardew Valley visual assets and game-driven effects only. No AI-generated art is included.[/b]
[b]Farmer’s End does not use AI, an LLM, or any other generative system while Stardew Valley is running.[/b]
Threat progression, monster pressure, Leaders, Breach reinforcements, Monster Ambush, RUMBLE, damage changes, and rewards are all controlled through predefined rules and programmed randomisation.
AI does not generate monsters, maps, combat behaviour, encounters, rewards, dialogue, or other gameplay content at runtime.
